headline: Council adopted an order seeking a draft ordinance with higher noise fines, and denied a 5-6 order on permanent public bathrooms.
summary: Members approved grants of $15,000 and $244,500 and a $162,500 transfer for bond costs. They denied the public bathroom order 5-6 and placed a license hearing proposal on file 7-3. Many other orders were adopted, and several requests were referred to committees.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 15, 2026 meeting 11-0.
Referred requests to make Midgley Ave. and Esper Ave. public to the Planning Board 10-0.
Referred the request for a guardrail at 101 Plantation St. to the Public Works Committee 10-0.
Set a public hearing for October 6, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. on the Charter Communications conduit request at 135 Kenberma Rd. 10-0.
Confirmed the appointments of Echo Louissaint-Collins and Sharon Boateng to the Advisory Commission on Youth 10-0.
Referred the Burncoat School Building Project report to the Education Committee.
Approved a $15,000 grant from the Greater Worcester Community Foundation 11-0.
Approved a $244,500 grant from the Massachusetts Cultural Council 11-0.
Approved moving $162,500 to cover costs of the $10,500,000 general obligation bond and $36,248,342 bond anticipation notes 11-0.
Approved a $21,000 transfer for a heavy vehicle exclusion study for Lake Avenue and Hamilton Street 11-0.
Approved $35,000 for radar speed feedback signs on Belmont Street and Plantation Street 11-0.
Ordained amendments to the salary ordinance for three positions 11-0.
Asked the City Solicitor for a draft ordinance raising noise fines, adopted 8-1.
Placed on file the order on public hearings before the License Commission for one-day event licenses, 7-3.
Asked for a report on staffing two officers per patrol car, as amended.
Asked the Chief Development Officer to develop a New Homeowner and Tenant Summit.
Asked the City Manager to develop a policy standardizing mitigation and community benefits for new developments.
Asked the City Manager to use opioid settlement funds to hire public bathroom monitoring and maintenance staff.
Motion to hold the permanent public bathroom order under privilege failed 4-7.
Denied the amended order to identify permanent public bathroom locations and porta-potty sites 5-6.
Held the order on Optiline Enterprises work at 274 Franklin St. under privilege 11-0.
Asked the Commissioner of Public Works to fill potholes on Oriental St. as soon as possible.
Asked the Commissioner of Public Works to make emergency sidewalk repairs at 2 Intervale Rd. 11-0.
Asked for a report on safe passage for students near Columbus Park Preparatory School 11-0.
Asked the Police Chief for more traffic enforcement near Worcester State University and May Street Elementary School 10-0.
Asked the City Manager to determine who is responsible for mowing land near Doherty Memorial High School 11-0.
Asked for a report on a Homeless Strategic Plan, adopted 11-0.
Asked the Commissioner of Health and Human Services for a Municipal ID program report, as amended, 11-0.
Asked the City Manager to work with the Police Chief and school superintendent on a youth helmet pilot program 11-0.

1. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

participated in the meeting remotely until his arrival in the Chamber at 7:32 P.M.
4. PROCLAMATIONS, ACKNOWLEDGMENTS, MOMENTS OF SILENCE
4a. MOMENT OF SILENCE in memory of Paul J. Giorgio, who passed away on Saturday , 
September 26, 2026 at the age of 75. Mr. Giogio was a prominent figure in national, state 
and local politics, and was the creator of Pulse Magazine, a publication that for more 
than two decades served as a cultural voice, as well as a platform for arts, entertainment 
and dining in the city.
4b. Mayor Petty read a Proclamation declaring the week of October 1, 2026 through October 
8, 2026 as the Week Without Driving in the City of Worcester. Mayor Petty also 
recognized Councilor Bilotta, who read a statement on behalf of WalkBike Worcester , 
who accepted the Proclamation.
